subject.title: Stability, installer auth, runtime compatibility, and context-management improvements

question: Should #86567 stay open as a coordination umbrella while maintainers split it into focused dashboard-auth, OpenAI/Codex-auth, runtime-compatibility, final-turn, and context-hygiene workstreams?
rationale: The issue is actionable but spans security, installer, provider, runtime, and session-state ownership; automation cannot safely choose the product boundary or credential-persistence policy.

options.title: Split and coordinate
options.body: Keep the umbrella open for tracking, route each concrete slice to an owner-backed issue or PR, and close the umbrella only after the linked slices cover the original acceptance criteria.

options.title: Close in favor of narrower issues
options.body: Close this umbrella only if maintainers decide the linked dashboard-auth and turn-completion issues are the complete canonical tracking surface for the remaining work.

options.title: Define one broad project owner
options.body: Assign a single maintainer to turn the field report into a cross-cutting project plan before any repair lane starts.

recommendation.title: Split and coordinate
recommendation.body: Keep the umbrella open for tracking, route each concrete slice to an owner-backed issue or PR, and close the umbrella only after the linked slices cover the original acceptance criteria.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent broad area history and merged PR metadata make this the best available coordinator signal among the identified owners, though the final split needs security and macOS owner input.
